statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-116318 (PostgreSQL pg_dump not-null constraint name allows SQL injection) affects only PostgreSQL 18: the PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116318/, says versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected and lists 18.7 as the only fixed release, and the CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116318, lists only major version 18 as affected. The flaw is in how pg_dump prints the name of a child table's own NOT NULL constraint on an inherited column. Named NOT NULL constraints exist only from PostgreSQL 18, which stores column NOT NULL specifications in pg_constraint (see the PostgreSQL 18 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.0/); the fix, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/d7344264584bd66ff4dcb038c6f57e773b8abc3a, changes that output in src/bin/pg_dump/pg_dump.c and is marked back-patch through 18. At every PostgreSQL 17 release this owner publishes (REL_17_7 through REL_17_12; for example https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_17_12/src/bin/pg_dump/pg_dump.c), pg_dump.c tracks no per-column NOT NULL constraint names and never prints a CONSTRAINT name NOT NULL clause. The pg_dump program in every published DHI postgresql17-client build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports its 17.x release and does not contain the "CONSTRAINT %s NOT NULL" format string, which the postgresql18-client pg_dump does contain. None of the Alpine patches applied in the 17.12-r0 APKBUILD touch pg_dump. The 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/, do not list this CVE. Alpine's postgresql17 17.12-r0 secfixes list CVE-2026-116318 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-116318), but upstream's own advisory places PostgreSQL 17 outside the affected range.
